name: Captain Technocast Limited
summary: Established casting operations have grown, but FY2026 trading/acquisition changes obscure comparable organic growth. A funded sum-of-parts stress model does not support the ₹235 dated quote; subsidiary loan recovery and very thin observed trading are decisive risks.
identity_note: Captain Technocast Limited, INE931X01010, BSE540652. IPO prospectus supports SME origin; October19 interoperability ST row identifies BSE listing, 23,220,100 shares and750-share lot. No main-board migration established. Technical series dates are not the 2017 IPO date. [S1][S7][S91][S92]

quote.kind: secondary dated close, not live or assured executable

score_note: NS aggregates: REV organic-comparability evidence missing; IAS also lacks complete implementation L. All other canonical factors and linked annual scenarios are assessed; no missing weight is redistributed.

gates.reason: Related-party allocation and Vartis disposal require scrutiny, but a near-book sale price, shareholder-approval disclosure and unmodified audit are counterevidence to an unsupported abuse allegation. Full independent valuation and receipt are not available.

Main audited statements support historical and modeled balances. FY 2021 comparative cash-flow changes, current note-table inconsistencies and unbridged organic/trading revenue prevent a precise comparable REV factor; do not replace audited main statements with inconsistent summary tables.

Base requires ₹5.1061 crore additional external borrowing across separately modeled entities; availability is not verified. X2 parent-loan recovery is impaired even in the illustrative base. The no-new-debt sensitivity fails financing.

Latest recovered trade is October 9, not October 19; only26/60 provider rows and no live depth, spread or complete BSE restriction check. Even observed-only turnover suggests slow exits. A quoted price is not implementation clearance.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Not a demonstrated compounder and not a supported purchase at the dated ₹235 quote. The casting parent is a real, profitable operating business, not a story-only shell: FY 2026 parent revenue was ₹108.3971 crore and PAT ₹10.1837 crore. However, new stock-in-trade purchases, the acquired-and-sold Vartis perimeter, weak returns on some group capital and an expensive implied growth path materially change the investment conclusion. The separately financed parent/X2/Metcast/Castech model produces bear/base/bull terminal prices ₹27.24/₹104.68/₹229.20, before execution costs. These are analyst scenarios, not targets or management guidance. A missing reliable organic-growth bridge leaves REV, BQS and GQS NS, while the remaining operating factors are explicitly assessed rather than all being withheld. IAS remains NS because Q and executable liquidity are unresolved. [S1][S2][S8][S9][S10][S95]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Cutoff 20 October 2026. Nonfinancial manufacturing/trading archetype; amounts are ₹crore unless stated. March 2026 audited openings feed five annual periods ending March 2031; part of the first modeled year precedes the October 9 investor quote and is a conditional nowcast, not an observed October balance. The issuer was incorporated20 July 2010 and converted to public status21 April 2017. The2017 prospectus identifies a BSE SME issue; the October 19 interoperability record corroborates ISIN, 23,220,100 shares and lot750. No migration was established. Its ST market-status code is a technical price-discovery status, not an assertion of suspension or clearance. Historical statutory accounts have medium confidence after stated reconciliations; forward assumptions are medium-to-low, organic comparability and implementation low. G1/G2/G3 are conditional and G4 is an unresolved execution hold. No negative surveillance finding or blanket legal clearance is invented from an absent result. [S1][S7][S91][S92][S95]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV NS, DUR 5, CAP 5, CASH 6, BAL 5, EXEC 5 and EARN 6. Business evidence is ordinary-to-mixed, not automatically exceptional because reported growth is high. BQS known weighted contribution4.50 at 88% coverage gives mathematical bounds4.62–5.70, not a renormalized score. GQS contribution3.25 at 60% coverage gives3.65–7.25. REV is specifically missing because group acquisition/perimeter changes and parent trading obscure comparable demand, not because growth is weak. R 1 follows the reference return well below a15% hurdle; D 2 reflects severe loss and refinancing paths; P 1 reflects the extreme reverse-growth burden. L is NS: observed-only liquidity calculations are supplied but missing provider sessions cannot be declared zero or assumed complete. IAS known contribution0.85 at 65% coverage gives1.20–4.35 bounds with Q/L unresolved. No governance override or persistent cash/capital cap is applied. Exact weights and evidence are attached.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The parent uses lost-wax investment casting: tooling/wax preparation, assembly, ceramic coating, casting, finishing and quality control. Tool design/process discipline and customer qualification matter, but disclosed in-house know-how and no current R&D spend do not establish proprietary technology. FY 2026 parent exports₹41.0511 crore were approximately37.9% of revenue, versus₹33.0964 crore previously; domestic sales and trading contribute the remainder. Working capital is material: parent inventory₹10.6311 crore and receivables₹18.3961 crore. The2017 top-ten customer share96.27% is a historical concentration warning, not a current concentration statistic. [S1][S7]

Group scope is not interchangeable with the parent. Captain Castech is70%-owned and still reports nil revenue/profit; X2 Valves is70%-owned with ₹14.6480 crore sales and ₹0.6512 crore PAT; Captain Metcast is a20% associate with ₹23.5798 crore sales and ₹1.2312 crore PAT. Vartis was51%-acquired from 1 April 2025 and subsequently approved for disposal. Group revenue cannot be decomposed by simply subtracting Vartis gross₹29.2862 crore, because intercompany dealings are eliminated. The model therefore uses parent operations and separate economic interests, not a guessed continuing-group revenue subtraction. [S1][S2][S8][S9][S10]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
MOAT 5 means useful but contestable production relationships, not a structural monopoly. Qualification, tooling accuracy, rejection control and reliable delivery could create switching friction; the reviewed record does not quantify current retention, customer concentration, rejection rates or price premiums. Many suppliers can perform investment casting, and metal/energy inputs plus customer bargaining constrain economics. Parent strict manufacturing EBITDA is₹13.6270 crore,12.57% of revenue, before separately disclosed export/packing/solar income; treating every other-income line as nonoperating would be too harsh. [S1][S7]

Primary-source comparators provide economic context, not a valuation shortcut. Investment & Precision Castings FY 2025 standalone revenue ₹165.0737 crore and calculated strict EBITDA margin13.63% show a comparable process can produce ordinary margins; its management describes aerospace approvals and capital intensity, which cannot be transferred to Captain. Steelcast FY 2026 reports₹438.62 crore revenue and 30.64% EBITDA margin, but heavier industrial castings, scale and customer mix differ materially. Those businesses demonstrate both competition and wide economic dispersion. No peer multiple has been fabricated or used to justify Captain’s quote. [S11][S12]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Group audited revenue FY 2021–FY 2026 is₹42.5995/50.4926/59.0874/64.2291/92.1562/129.8684 crore. Annual additions are₹7.8931/8.5948/5.1417/27.9271/37.7122 crore; reported five-year CAGR24.97% and latest growth40.92% are not organic growth. Metcast changed from subsidiary to associate in September 2021, X2 contributed to later group expansion, and Vartis entered FY 2026. The parent’s five-year reported CAGR20.54% uses₹42.5995→108.3971 crore, but FY 2026 contains₹22.4507 crore new stock-in-trade purchases and ₹26.888 crore purchases from Vartis inclusive of taxes. Purchase cost cannot be subtracted as though it were exactly resale revenue. [S1][S3][S4][S5][S6]

Exports rising24.0% and the parent’s FY 2025 revenue ₹81.5664 crore are positive operating cross-checks, but do not reconstruct domestic casting volumes, pass-through prices or trading gross margins. Earlier FY 2023 parent comparatives also move approximately₹0.10 crore between revenue and other income while total income is similar; the group series is retained as disclosed. REV therefore remains NS rather than selecting a flattering window or applying an arbitrary one-point acquisition penalty. A segment/volume-price-trading bridge is the specific missing evidence. This does not erase the clearly positive reported expansion.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
DUR 5 recognizes export access and casting/valve applications, tempered by unverified capacity utilization and customer qualification. The2017 prospectus planned800 MT capacity and 750 MT FY 2020 output, but a current audited production/utilization reconciliation was not found; old projections are not current achievements. FY 2026 cash capex₹19.1138 crore exceeded group CFO₹8.2398 crore. Castech remains pre-commercial; X2 reports₹7.6125 crore CWIP in its ageing schedule, including₹4.0871 crore older than one year, while the group reports₹8.1493 crore total CWIP. These are not the same scope. [S1][S7][S8][S9]

CAP 5 reflects mixed, immature capital returns rather than treating all CWIP as free future growth. Strict group NOPAT at a normalized25% tax rate increases₹7.8089→11.0854 crore; invested capital including NCI, all reported debt and CWIP, less cash, increases₹45.5584→73.8123 crore. The incremental proxy is11.60%, around/below an analyst12–16% capital-cost range, not a certified organic ROIC because acquisitions, investment income and timing affect it. Excluding quoted investments/associate loans would artificially improve the stewardship picture. The base separately funds parent capex, X2 commissioning and Metcast growth; Castech receives no invented commercial sales. X2’s base parent-loan recovery is only₹2.2675 crore of ₹8.4 crore despite additional external funding. GQS remains NS solely because underlying REV is unresolved, not because remaining factors were left unperformed.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Anil Bhalu and Shailesh Bhut lead the operating business. FY 2026 disclosed salaries₹0.4200/₹0.4380 crore compare with ₹0.5200/₹0.5380 crore FY 2025, so remuneration did not mechanically rise with profits; proposed future caps are not actual payments. The annual report states promoter holdings are unencumbered as of its reporting period. Summing28 named promoter positions gives15,020,100 shares,64.69% of current shares; it is not a fresh October pledge certificate. FY 2025 issued1.4 million shares before the April 2025 one-for-one bonus; the bonus doubles shares without raising cash and is not economic dilution by itself. [S1][S6]

Allocation needs scrutiny. Captain Polyplast investment cost₹10.8 crore versus March quoted market₹8.1375 crore was not written down under management’s temporary-diminution assessment; that judgment is not proof of fraud. Related fixed-asset purchases from Polyplast total₹8.1429 crore inclusive of taxes. Vartis51% cost₹1.3872 crore was proposed for sale at ₹1.958808 crore to named buyers including Ashokbhai K. Bhut, identified as promoter group. The price is approximately1.008× the share of disclosed March net assets, counterevidence to an automatic unfair-price allegation. The annual report says shareholders approved the sale17 June 2026 and it is no longer a subsidiary; actual receipt/closing and the full May 4 independent valuation were not verified. [S1][S2]

The group auditor’s opinion is unmodified, while the audit-trail paragraph reports Vartis software did not operate the trail for all transactions throughout the year. This is a disclosed control exception, not a finding of tampering. Other current notes contain inconsistent loan and profit-allocation tables; primary main statements govern the calculations. Promises-versus-delivery is mixed:2017 working-capital-funded casting expansion led to higher sales; X2 now produces revenue but retains substantial CWIP; Castech still has none; Vartis was acquired then exited within the following reporting cycle. GOV 5/EXEC 5 reflect those concrete tensions, not generic reassurance.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Five-year FY 2022–FY 2026 CFO totals₹29.7219 crore versus owners’ PAT₹29.1812 crore,1.019×; including minority profits gives roughly0.98×, a better group-scope cross-check. Cumulative cash capex₹31.5795 crore makes CFO less capex negative₹1.8576 crore before acquisitions/investments. FY 2026 alone CFO/PAT before minority interest is approximately0.66× and CFO less capex is negative₹10.8740 crore. Do not classify Castech’s parent-loan repayment as customer conversion: it replaced parent funding with other shareholder/director borrowing. CASH 6 recognizes decent cumulative realization but current investment/WC strain. [S1][S4][S5][S6][S8]

Group March debt₹20.0577 crore less cash₹1.2730 crore gives net debt₹18.7847 crore. Strict EBITDA₹17.4164 crore gives1.08× net leverage and strict EBIT₹14.7805 crore covers reported interest7.64×; neither ratio captures all associate debt or proves access to new facilities. X2 and Metcast current debt maturities₹0.307692/₹0.556604 crore are reclassified from their OCL into model debt, not treated twice. Parent gross current provisions₹3.7495 crore settle once; government advances remain in broad WC, without a second invented tax recovery. X2 net tax₹0.012181 crore settles; Metcast’s₹0.039267 crore net tax-asset recovery is conditional and has a delayed-recovery sensitivity. Other expense/statutory/employee balances already in WC are not paid twice. All opening claims are mapped in the model. [S1][S9][S10]

Historical reliability caveats are specific: FY 2021 CFO₹1.9707 crore originally becomes₹1.0524 crore in the FY 2022 comparative, alongside financing reclassification; no silent splice is made. FY 2022 closing-cash presentation differs₹0.01 crore from components. Current note34 associate loans conflict with notes13/36, and note35’s profit attribution does not cleanly reconcile to the main P&L. These limit precision; they do not establish fabricated accounts. X2, Castech and Metcast also disclose that retirement leave-encashment obligations are not provided because they cannot quantify them; the parent charges leave when paid. No missing actuarial amount is invented or treated as proven zero. A separate analyst cash stress tests additional employee claims without presenting it as a legal or actuarial estimate. [S8][S9][S10] Current group receivables₹23.7051 crore include₹0.8948 crore aged1–2 years, concentrated in X2, which the bear case impairs noncash and then funds replacement WC correctly.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Dated October 9 close₹235 ×2.32201 crore shares implies₹545.67235 crore market capitalization, approximately46.95× FY 2026 owners’ PAT. The undated input snapshot is not used as a current quote. The sum-of-parts model separately finances parent operations,70%-owned X2,20%-owned Metcast and 70%-owned Castech. It subtracts each entity’s external and internal debt before minority allocation, then separately values only the parent’s recoverable loan claim. Thus neither subsidiary PAT nor carrying-value investments are double capitalized. Vartis sale proceeds enter parent cash once, with 25% tax on the assumed gain; no future Vartis profit or second terminal sale value is added. Polyplast terminal recovery₹6/8.1375/10.8 crore is an assumption anchored to March cost/market information, not an October market quote. [S1][S2][S8][S9][S10][S95]

Parent bear/base/bull growth is−10% then0–3%/8%/15%, EBITDA margins10%/14%/16%, WC28%/22%/19% of revenue and exit EBIT multiples6/10/14. Base14% margin allows some recurring export/packing/solar economics relative to strict12.57% manufacturing EBITDA; FX gains are not independently extrapolated. X2/Metcast have their own revenue, margins, capex, DA, WC, interest and tax schedules. Existing interest-free intercompany loans remain outstanding; outside debt costs12%, including half-year new draws. Castech is a separately funded no-revenue maintenance/NAV case, not a free option. Each scenario includes cash/debt rollforwards, shareholder claims, minority interests and no invented dividends. [S1][S8][S9][S10]

Bear/base/bull terminal₹27.2395/104.6805/229.2013 imply annualized−38.23%/−16.54%/−0.56% from October 9 to March 2031. Additional external borrowing₹17.6431/5.1061/8.2998 crore is conditional, not approved funding. Base components include parent operating equity₹227.2621 crore, X2 equity nil and loan recovery₹2.2675 crore, Metcast equity share₹2.1916 crore plus parent loan ₹3.05 crore, and Castech parent recovery₹0.1604 crore. Reverse15% hurdle requires parent revenue approaching₹810.69 crore, about49.54% annual growth for five years under base margins/multiple with scaled reinvestment, far above an ordinary continuation. Margin/multiple, delayed tax recovery, no-disposal receipt, investment loss, no-new-debt and DCF discount sensitivities are attached. No likelihood weighting, guaranteed exit or precise fair-value claim is assigned.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest counterargument is not that casting demand disappears: a decent operating business can still be a poor investment at a price requiring exceptional compounding. Parent growth slows, margin falls, WC stays high and X2’s older receivables lose value just as commissioned assets need debt service. The bear writes off parent/X2/Metcast receivables₹1.83961/0.894812/0.435446 crore as noncash charges, reduces recoverable opening WC and funds the replacement required by future activity. It does not count both impairment and the same cash loss twice. Terminal₹27.24 is an88.41% price loss, even assuming₹17.64 crore new external funding remains available; without new debt the model flags financing failure, not a valid return forecast. Group investment/loan recoverability, supplier credit and loan-on-demand terms can transmit stress across entities. [S1][S8][S9][S10]

A more severe combined margin/WC/disposal/investment stress is supplied, with no invented financing commitment. The principal thesis-break variables are persistent sub12% parent margins, WC above28% of sales, inability to refinance X2/associate debt, failed Vartis receipt and customer concentration/collections. A low traded float or quotation staleness can make paper downside non-executable. D 2 does not assert imminent default; it records that current-price shareholder protection is weak under a linked plausible stress.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Neither5× nor10× is demonstrated by the reviewed business plan. At fixed current shares, fivefold price requires₹1,175 and tenfold₹2,350. The cash-linked reverse test scales parent capex and depreciation with revenue and retains base subsidiary assumptions, margins and exit multiple: it requires approximately84.11%/112.44% annual parent revenue growth, reaching₹2,292.88/₹4,690.53 crore, with calculated additional external borrowing₹118.71/₹355.66 crore. Those numbers are mathematical requirements, not credible capacity/customer commitments. No verified utilization, tooling qualification, offtake or financing package supports that scale. Even the ordinary bull reaches only₹229.20, below the dated starting quote. A large quoted multibagger potential cannot substitute for demonstrated per-share economics and funding. [S1][S7][S8][S9][S10]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: 1. Obtain a parent casting-versus-trading revenue, volume and margin bridge; this is the REV-score unblocker. 2. Track export revenue against₹41.0511 crore FY 2026 and disclose customer concentration; unexplained loss of a major account weakens DUR. 3. Test parent EBITDA margin against12.57% strict/14% modeled, identifying export/solar/FX separately. 4. Monitor group CFO/PAT and annual cash capex: FY 2026 CFO₹8.2398 crore versus capex₹19.1138 crore cannot persist without funding. 5. Collect X2’s₹0.8948 crore aged1–2-year receivables; any rollover or settlement discount is a cash-quality warning. 6. Verify X2 commissioning,₹7.6125 crore CWIP and parent₹8.4 crore loan recoverability. 7. Require Castech commercial revenue or a funded maintenance/exit plan, not just net assets. 8. Verify Vartis settlement₹1.958808 crore and valuation rationale; report rather than assume receipt. 9. Reconcile associate loans/current-tax balances and all maturities before an updated model. 10. Obtain complete BSE trading/restriction data and live lot/depth before considering any position. Thresholds are research tripwires, not automatic trade instructions.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Evidence-led watch/avoid-at-dated-price conclusion, with implementation on hold. This is not an integrity-failure classification: there is no substantiated fraud finding in this review. Reported growth and positive accumulated CFO are real positives, but the organic-growth bridge, allocation discipline and price-implied burden prevent compounder certification. All supportable operating factors and full financing scenarios are complete; unresolved REV and L remain genuinely missing rather than replaced with neutral scores. The base misses the15% hurdle by more than30 percentage points, and even the bull does not recover the dated quote. A materially lower price, independently verified cash/loan recoveries and evidence of substantially better recurring margins/growth could change valuation, but price alone cannot cure cash, accounting or execution uncertainty. No order, suitable personal position size or assured exit is implied.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence includes2017 prospectus, FY 2021/22/24/25/26 annual accounts, May 2026 postal ballot and three audited subsidiary/associate statements. The issuer FY 2024 annual-link currently supplies an annual-return form; the actual financial report was recovered from the original BSE filing mirrored by Business Standard. Do not cite the wrong document as an annual financial audit. Direct BSE voting/scrutinizer attachments returned Access Denied HTML and were not retried or treated as read; the annual report itself supports the approval disclosure. Full independent Vartis valuation, actual sale receipt, current customer/capacity data and organic/trading split remain missing. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5][S6][S7][S8][S9][S10][S96]

All forecasts, tax rates, terminal multiples, loan-priority/recovery assumptions and funding are analyst assumptions. Intercompany claims stay outstanding and receive value only after modeled external claims; legal ranking could differ. Historical group cash/earnings and parent standalone values are labeled separately. The market ledger uses secondary OHLCV, not actual BSE traded value; absent rows are unknown, not automatically zero. On the26 observed60-window sessions, low×volume mean ₹363,679 and median ₹211,500 imply₹5 lakh exit118.20/47.28/23.64 days at 2%/5%/10% participation using the lower observed statistic. A conditional missing-as-zero test has zero median and no finite estimate, but is not asserted as fact. Latest lot750 costs₹176,250; two lots₹352,500 and three₹528,750 cannot exactly match₹5 lakh. Current spreads, circuits, counterparty depth and BSE surveillance are not verified. [S91][S92][S95]

GOV.reason: Disclosed related allocation, inconsistent notes and brief Vartis holding period are material concerns; near-book disposal, unmodified opinion and lower actual remuneration counter an unsupported abuse conclusion.

MOAT.reason: Qualified process/customer relationships are useful but contestable; ordinary relative margins and no quantified pricing power or retention preclude a strong-moat score.

REV.reason: Reported growth is known, but acquisitions and new trading purchases materially obscure comparable demand. No reliable organic/volume-price bridge, so no numerical starting CAGR is substituted.

DUR.reason: Established export access and multiple applications provide runway, with unverified utilization, customer concentration and immature valve/casting projects.

CAP.reason: CWIP/investment-inclusive incremental proxy11.60% is around/below12–16% capital-cost range; mature parent and immature group cohorts are mixed, not proven durable excess economics.

CASH.reason: Five-year group conversion is near1x after minority alignment; current capex deficit and aged X2 receipts prevent a strong-cycle score, but persistent poor CFO is not established.

BAL.reason: Reported leverage/coverage manageable, but separately leveraged subsidiaries, demand loans and conditional additional funding create meaningful stress sensitivity.

EXEC.reason: Parent growth and X2 revenue demonstrate delivery, offset by Castech nil turnover, aged CWIP and rapid Vartis exit; forecasts are not milestones achieved.

EARN.reason: Strict EBIT grew strongly alongside PAT, with bonus-adjusted per-share progress; new trading, acquisition scope and recurring versus FX/solar items make quality mixed.

Q.reason: BQS is incomplete because REV is unresolved.

R.reason: Base annualized return−16.54% versus15% hurdle gives−31.54pp spread under explicit funded assumptions; this falls below−10pp.

D.reason: Bear price loss88.41% despite conditional new debt; no-new-debt case fails. Current-price recovery support is weak without asserting imminent default.

valuation.formula: Entity CFO=operating PAT+DA+noncash impairment−delta recoverable WC. Old claims, capex, disposal taxes, new debt and repayments bridge cash. New debt has half-year interest. Subsidiary equity is EV+cash−external−internal debt, floored atzero; parent loan recovery is capped by value after external claims. Ownership applies only to residual equity, never to the parent loan. Sum parent net operating value, recoverable loans, owned equity and quoted-investment recovery once.
